Area Under the Curve (AUC) by the trapezoidal rule

Source: R/auc.r
ks_auc.Rd

Computes AUC from concentration–time data using the linear or log-linear trapezoidal method. Handles grouped data via a character vector of grouping column names.

Usage

ks_auc(data, by = NULL, val, time, type = c("trapez", "log-trapez"))

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble.

by

Character vector of grouping column names, e.g. c("usubjid", "trt"). NULL (default) computes a single AUC across the whole dataset.

val

Unquoted name of the concentration (value) column.

time

Unquoted name of the time column (numeric).

type

AUC method: "trapez" (linear, default) or "log-trapez" (log-linear).

Value

  • When by = NULL: a single numeric value.

  • When by is provided: a data.frame with one row per group and an AUC column appended to the grouping columns.

Details

Linear trapezoid (type = "trapez"): $$AUC_i = \frac{C_i + C_{i+1}}{2} \cdot (t_{i+1} - t_i)$$

Log-linear trapezoid (type = "log-trapez"): $$AUC_i = \frac{C_{i+1} - C_i}{\ln C_{i+1} - \ln C_i} \cdot (t_{i+1} - t_i)$$

The log-linear method is preferred during elimination phases where concentrations decline exponentially. It requires strictly positive concentrations; when two consecutive values are equal or one is \(\leq 0\) the interval automatically falls back to the linear rule.

Rows are sorted by c(by, time) before computing so the caller does not need to pre-sort the data.

See also

ks_auc for the vectorised helper

Examples

## Single subject — linear trapezoid
pk1 <- data.frame(conc = c(0, 4, 2, 1), time = c(0, 1, 2, 4))
ks_auc(pk1, val = conc, time = time)
#> [1] 8

## Two subjects — grouped
pk2 <- data.frame(
  id   = c("A","A","A","B","B","B"),
  conc = c(0, 4, 1,  0, 6, 2),
  time = c(0, 1, 2,  0, 1, 2)
)
ks_auc(pk2, by = "id", val = conc, time = time)
#>   id AUC
#> 1  A 4.5
#> 2  B 7.0
